title: The Inadequacy of Offline LLM Evaluations: A Need to Account for Personalization in Model Behavior

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing stateless (offline) benchmark evaluations of language models against stateful (field) evaluations conducted by real users to demonstrate the inadequacy and lack of representativeness of standard AI evaluation methods.

Measuring output heterogeneity and variations in benchmark scores (e.g., MMLU, ETHICS) when models are prompted through personalized interfaces utilizing user history, memory banks, and simulated 'sock puppet' profiles.

Stratifying a field evaluation with 800 real users across intersectional demographic groups (Black women, Black men, White women, White men) and utilizing a survey instrument to test whether the model inferred race, culture, or gender from the user's name or profile.
